Stage 1 component distributions. The figure uses layer 1 molecular data. (A) Component 1
sample-coordinate distribution. (B) Component 2 sample-coordinate distribution. Facets show
components 1-2 in decomposition order; stored densities summarize sample-coordinate
distributions; baseline marks show sample coordinates; dotted vertical lines mark zero.
Categorical metadata is shown by density fills and outlines; outline line type and
baseline-point shape repeat group identity. The analysis unit is independent biological
observation; the design is cross-sectional; the estimand is the descriptive distribution of
sample coordinates. No component-selection threshold is applied. This descriptive gallery does
not rank or nominate a biological coordinate.

This descriptive gallery does not rank or nominate a biological coordinate.
Stage 1 decomposition coordinates. The figure uses molecular layers layer 1, layer 2. Facets
identify molecular layers; points show component 1 sample coordinates rank-ordered within each
layer; the dotted horizontal line marks zero. Point colours and point shapes encode categorical
planted group. The subtitle reports the stored synthetic ground-truth angle for component 1.
The analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the descriptive sample coordinate on component 1. No component-selection threshold
is applied. This display does not select a component or establish biological interpretation.

Density-derived quasi-potential landscape. The figure uses molecular layers layer 1, layer 2.
The black curve shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component
1. Coloured points identify categorical planted group and show sample coordinates in directly
labelled baseline rows; row position and text provide non-colour group identification; no
metadata stems are drawn. Critical-point symbols and barrier-height segments are omitted. The
analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the density-derived quasi-potential along the selected component. No calibrated
critical-point or barrier threshold is applied. The landscape is an exploratory description and
does not by itself establish a biological state transition.

Density-derived quasi-potential landscape. The figure uses layer 1 molecular data. The black
curve shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component 1.
Coloured points identify categorical planted group and show sample coordinates in directly
labelled baseline rows; row position and text provide non-colour group identification; no
metadata stems are drawn. Small open circles mark stored stable wells directly on the curve.
Small red diamonds mark stored unstable barriers directly on the curve. Dashed vertical
segments show point-estimate barrier heights. The vertical display is focused on the stored
critical-point and barrier-height range; higher low-density tails continue beyond the panel.
The analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the density-derived quasi-potential along the selected component. Critical-point
classifications and barrier heights are point estimates without uncertainty. No calibrated
critical-point or barrier threshold is applied. The landscape is an exploratory description and
does not by itself establish a biological state transition.
